Chapter 12: The Call to Service—Leadership, Responsibility, and Making a Difference.
When you think about leadership, what comes to mind? Maybe titles, positions, or having authority over others. But, what if true leadership is really about service? About being responsible, and putting others first?
The Sunan Ibn Majah is packed with stories that flip our usual ideas about power. Instead of seeking control, these teachings offer a vision of leadership that's built on humility and genuine care.
Imagine a community struggling with a tough decision. Their leader could have just made the call himself, but he didn’t. He brought everyone together, listened carefully to their worries, and worked to find common ground. He remembered the example set by the Prophet—real leaders serve, they consult, and they act with fairness. In the end, even though the decision was hard, everyone accepted it. And that experience made the community stronger.
The hadith remind us that leadership isn’t limited to people in charge. Every one of us has a role to play in our own circles—whether you’re a parent, a teacher, a neighbor, or a friend. There’s a beautiful story about a woman who, even without wealth or influence, became a pillar in her community simply by being kind and supportive. Her quiet actions inspired others to pitch in and make a difference too.
One theme that keeps coming up is responsibility—what’s called amanah. The Prophet encouraged everyone to fulfill their duties honestly, to keep their promises, and to care for anyone who’s been entrusted to them. Think about the young man who was put in charge of a small project. He worked hard, asked for advice, and made sure no one was left out. The project was a success, and he realized that leadership is really about trust, not control.
There’s also a clear warning against chasing power just for the sake of it. Take the story of a man who campaigned hard for a position of authority, only to end up feeling overwhelmed and alone. When he looked for help, he was reminded—leadership is a burden, not a privilege. If you want it, approach it with humility and a real desire to serve others.
Most of us don’t realize how much impact those small, everyday acts of leadership can have—listening to a friend, helping a neighbor, or standing up for what’s right. The teachings in Sunan Ibn Majah encourage us to lead by example, to serve with humility, and to make a difference wherever we can.
So, the next time you wonder what it means to be a leader, remember—it’s not about the title, it’s about the responsibility. It’s about serving others, making choices with integrity, and inspiring those around you. That’s how real change happens.
